1. Core Clinical Tension: A 60-year-old woman presents with a 2-year history of a slowly expanding, painless, soft, mobile mass in the right calf originally presumed to be an intramuscular lipoma. Isolated soft tissue echinococcosis of the lower extremity without visceral (hepatic or pulmonary) involvement is exceptionally rare and can easily be misdiagnosed as a benign mesenchymal tumor or synovial cyst.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission clinical assessment concludes after physical examination, screening abdominal ultrasound, and chest radiography ruling out visceral lesions, and calf ultrasonography showing the multivesicular cystic mass, prior to surgical incisional exploration, cyst evacuation, and anthelmintic therapy.
3. Differential Distinctions: Intramuscular lipoma, which was the initial clinical diagnosis, was ruled out when ultrasound demonstrated fluid-filled multivesicular cystic structures rather than homogenous hyperechoic adipose tissue. Popliteal (Baker) cyst or intramuscular hematoma/seroma was ruled out by the anatomical location in the mid-calf, absence of trauma, intact knee joint, and presence of multiple internal daughter cysts.
case_prompt:
A 60-year-old woman presented to the outpatient surgical clinic complaining of a painless mass in her right calf that had been present for two years. The mass was discovered incidentally two years earlier and had been diagnosed clinically at that time as a lipoma, for which no treatment was initiated. Over the preceding few months, the mass had gradually increased in size. Her medical history was notable for essential hypertension of ten years' duration managed with antihypertensive pharmacotherapy. Her past surgical history included a laparoscopic cholecystectomy ten years prior and an abdominal hysterectomy for uterine leiomyomas five years prior.

On physical examination, vital signs were normal. Examination of the right lower extremity revealed a 10 x 7 cm mass in the posterior compartment of the calf. The mass was soft, non-tender, fluctuant, and mobile from side to side without overlying warmth, erythema, or skin tethering.

Bedside and preoperative evaluation included a plain chest radiograph, which excluded pulmonary nodules or consolidations, and an abdominal ultrasound, which confirmed normal hepatic and visceral architecture without cysts or lesions. Soft tissue ultrasound of the right calf mass demonstrated a well-circumscribed cystic lesion containing multiple internal small cysts.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected clinically because of the chronic, soft, painless, and mobile nature of the calf mass, but excluded when soft tissue ultrasound demonstrated a complex multicystic fluid lesion containing internal small vesicles rather than uniform adipose tissue.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: diagnosed that time clinically as lipoma

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Baker Cyst / Intramuscular Hematoma or Seroma
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Synovial cysts and organizing hematomas can form cystic collections in the calf, but the absence of antecedent knee joint effusion or trauma, combined with the presence of multiple well-formed internal daughter cysts, excluded a simple fluid collection.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Ultrasound of the mass showed cystic lesion that contained multiple small cysts inside

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Ultrasound identification of a multilocular cystic architecture with internal vesicles in the gastrocnemius muscle, confirmed intraoperatively by surgical cystotomy revealing innumerable classic daughter cysts, definitively established isolated intramuscular echinococcosis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: During surgery cyst opened and was containing innumerable daughter cysts

editor_comments: Case presentation terminates cleanly after ultrasound description of multivesicular cyst, strictly withholding operative findings, chlorhexidine wash, and albendazole therapy.
